stages.title: Predict
stages.definition: Predict the resulting movement or sensation before the command is sent.

stages.title: Choose & do
stages.definition: The learner chooses a command for its expected result, and the body achieves that result.

stages.title: Repeat & keep
stages.definition: Repeat the chosen result in independent trials and retain it after further learning. Separately, saving and restoring the model must preserve the result.

stages.title: Changed conditions
stages.definition: Keep the ability when the starting posture, object, or surroundings change.

highlights.title: Eye-angle prediction
highlights.meaning: Where the eyes point 150 ms after an eye command, compared with assuming the eyes stay still, on a saved checkpoint (0% less error = no better than assuming stillness; 100% less = a perfect forecast). The test script chooses the eye commands, so this measures prediction, not a useful look. Next: choose and repeat a useful look.

highlights.title: Hand choice from memory
highlights.meaning: Hand-shape error with the learned hand stage against the same decision without it. The goal is the hand shape the planner itself chose from memory, on held-out bodies (bodies not used to fit the hand calibration). A round that fails keeps training paused for review (the operator's decision of Sep 25, 9:09 AM PDT).
